verdict.line: You lose if he chains Q's second stack into a W stun before you have Wither leveled; you win if you reach 15+ with Trinity Force online and a fat Q stack.

brief.thesis: K'Sante's Q (Ntofo Strikes) is on a 3.5s cooldown and builds stacks on hit — at 2 stacks it fires a shockwave that pulls you in, which is what turns a poke exchange into his all-in. Nasus has no dash or shield to answer that pull, so the entire lane is about denying him the second stack rather than trading damage. The 46.2% head-to-head over 117 games and K'Sante's lane/solo-kill edge both come from that one mechanic; nothing else in the kit is why you're behind.

theirWindow.when: He lands a Q poke on you in melee
theirWindow.what: He now has one stack. If you stay in his 450-range Q line he can land the second stack and pull you in, which chains straight into his Path Maker charge-up. Walk out of line-of-Q range immediately after the first hit instead of trading back.

yourWindow.when: His W (Path Maker, 14-10s CD) and E (Footwork, 10-8s CD) are both down
yourWindow.what: He has no dash, no shield, and no stun available. Drop Spirit Fire under him, stand in it, and land your highest-rank Q — this is the only window where he can't punish you for committing.

powerCurve.note: Q poke chains into stacks faster than your Q heals
R (All Out) adds a wall-knockback all-in
Trinity Force online, Wither peels his all-in
Stacked Q and ult drain swing fights

start.why: 50% win rate over 106 games — the regen and poke-block passive are built for exactly the Q-spam harass you're taking every 3.5 seconds.

boots.why: 50.5% win rate, 64.5% pick — the ability haste tightens your Q/W/E cooldowns, which matters more than armor since you're not out-tanking his burst early.

core.why: Converts your stacked Siphoning Strike into real on-hit damage and gives you the mobility to actually stick a Q before he resets space with Footwork.
The attack speed slow directly fights his Ntofo Strikes stacking tempo — slower stacks means fewer pull windows against you.
60% win rate on this exact path over 20 games — stacks Soul Eater lifesteal with heal amp so your sustain in extended trades outpaces his.

situational.when: he's building lifesteal and healing back the damage you land in trades
he's ahead and diving you repeatedly off All Out knockbacks
you need to stick to him or catch a split-push target in the sidelane

runes.keystoneWhy: You have no dash to dodge the Q-stack pull or the Path Maker charge — the healing and move speed proc is your only built-in way to disengage before the stun lands.

summoners.why: 51.4% win rate, the highest of the three combos in this matchup — Flash answers the W charge-up telegraph or a landed Q pull, and Teleport lets you reset waves safely while you stack Q instead of forcing even trades.

playing.title: Count his Q stacks, not his health
playing.detail: One stack is safe to walk away from; two stacks means the next hit pulls you in. Disengage after the first Q lands instead of trading back.

playing.title: Farm Q on low minions relentlessly
playing.detail: Siphoning Strike's permanent damage growth on kill is your entire scaling identity — every stack you miss is a stack he doesn't have to answer.

playing.title: Zone with Spirit Fire, don't chase with it
playing.detail: Drop E on the wave or on him when he commits to CS, not as a follow-up to a trade — the armor shred only matters if he's forced to stand in it.

playing.title: Save Wither for his all-in, not your engage
playing.detail: Once he's level 6+, hold W to decelerate him out of a Footwork-into-R combo rather than using it to start fights you can't finish.

playing.title: Watch the Path Maker charge animation
playing.detail: He takes reduced damage while charging before the dash that knocks back and stuns — sidestep during the windup rather than trading into it.

playing.title: Don't contest level 6-10 all-ins
playing.detail: All Out (R) through a wall into transformed abilities is a lane-losing window if you're even. Play for farm and ult uptime instead of answering his engage.

playing.title: Shift to split-push once Trinity Force lands
playing.detail: From level 11 on, your stacked Q and Fury of the Sands' health drain outscale his kit in extended 1v1s — look to force side lane pressure rather than all-in top.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, and summoner spells reflect measured win/pick rates from current-patch games; the lane-phase tactical reading — the Q-stack pull as the defining threat and the cooldown-window trade pattern — is my own analysis of the ability kits.
